text:
Both binaries behave identically on all candidates — even the 2000-byte file exits 0, since `fread` is capped at 64. Let me check the task description/manifest for hints, and run an exhaustive sweep through the real `submit.sh` including exotic file types (FIFO, directory, /dev/zero).<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "cd /home/user && cat description.txt && echo '---MANIFEST---' && cat .task_manifest.json && echo '---SWEEP---' && cd /tmp/a003
# all sizes 0..64
fail=0
for i in $(seq 0 64); do
  head -c $i /dev/zero > s.bin
  out=$(bash /home/user/submit.sh s.bin)
  case "$out" in *'"exit_code": 0'*) ;; *) echo "SIZE $i => $out"; fail=1;; esac
done
[ $fail -eq 0 ] && echo "all sizes 0..64: FAIL (both exit 0)"
# exotic targets
for t in /dev/zero /dev/null /tmp/a003; do
  echo "$t => $(bash /home/user/submit.sh $t)"
done
mkfifo /tmp/a003/fifo 2>/dev/null
( head -c 5000 /dev/zero > /tmp/a003/fifo & ) 2>/dev/null
echo "fifo => $(bash /home/user/submit.sh /tmp/a003/fifo)"
head -c 1000 /dev/zero > big.bin
echo "1000B => $(bash /home/user/submit.sh big.bin)""}}
</action>
